hero.title: OBJECTRADAR
hero.lead: Find nearby Bluetooth objects with intelligent BLE guidance

problem.title:
You know it's nearby.
But where is it?
problem.lead: You can know that a Bluetooth device is nearby without having a practical way to locate it precisely. ObjectRadar explores the Bluetooth information available to iOS to turn that signal into useful proximity guidance.

how-it-works.title: Three simple steps
how-it-works.lead: From scanning nearby Bluetooth devices, to identifying and tracking an object, ObjectRadar guides you through a simple workflow designed to help you find what you're looking for.

card1.title: Scan
card1.lead: Scan nearby Bluetooth devices and observe their signal strength.

card2.title: Identify
card2.lead: Identify the device of interest from the information available during the search.

card3.title: Track
card3.lead: Move through your environment and use proximity changes to narrow down the location.

use-cases.title: Designed around real situations
use-cases.lead: Explore how ObjectRadar can help you find different types of nearby Bluetooth devices and understand the steps involved in each search.

card1.title: Bluetooth trackers
card1.lead: Find a nearby tracker when conventional location information is not enough.

card2.title: Paired devices
card2.lead: Search for Bluetooth devices already associated with your iPhone.

card3.title: Other BLE devices
card3.lead: Explore nearby BLE devices beyond dedicated tracking tags.

card1.title: BLE scanning
card1.lead: Scan nearby Bluetooth advertisements and observe their signal strength.

card2.title: Device identification
card2.lead: Use available Bluetooth information to identify the device you are looking for.

card3.title: Proximity guidance
card3.lead: Use changes in signal strength to determine whether you are getting closer or farther away.

card4.title: Object association
card4.lead: Associate a detected Bluetooth device with the object you want to find.

card5.title: Local processing
card5.lead: Process the information needed for the search directly on the device.

card6.title: Privacy-focused design
card6.lead: Keep the search focused on local Bluetooth information without relying on a remote tracking service.

limitations.title: Bluetooth has physical limits.
limitations.lead: Bluetooth signal strength can help estimate proximity, but walls, furniture, orientation and other environmental factors can affect the result.

quote-box.title: Prototype statement
quote-box.lead: Closer / farther is more meaningful than an exact distance.

privacy.title: Designed to keep processing local.
privacy.lead: ObjectRadar is designed around local processing so the Bluetooth information used for the search can remain on the user's device.

question1.question: What can the application detect?
question1.answer: ObjectRadar scans nearby Bluetooth Low Energy advertisements and analyzes the information made available by the devices. Detection depends on the device, its advertising behavior and the information exposed by its Bluetooth protocol.

question2.question: How does proximity guidance work?
question2.answer: The application observes changes in Bluetooth signal strength while you move. These changes can indicate whether you are getting closer to or farther from a device, but they cannot provide a precise distance.

question3.question: Why can some Bluetooth devices remain invisible?
question3.answer: A device may not advertise continuously, may use a protocol that does not expose enough information, or may be affected by Bluetooth and environmental limitations.

question4.question: What are the limitations of Bluetooth tracking?
question4.answer: Bluetooth signal strength is affected by distance, obstacles, reflections, device orientation and the surrounding environment. Proximity guidance should therefore be understood as an indication rather than an exact measurement.
